narrative_events.details: Brahmā describes Sāma, an antyaja wrongdoer whose sight destroys piety. For wealth he murders twelve peaceful Brahmins, leaves their bodies in a cave and takes their possessions. Returning home on Māgha dark fourth at moonrise, he calls his son Gaṇeśa twice and eats with him after taking no food or water. Verse 13 explicitly says tasyaputro’sau dies that night; verse 14’s saḥ reaches Vaināyaka through the unintentional vow, and verse 16’s remaining merit produces the present Kṛtavīrya. The Sāma-versus-son death and rebirth referent is unresolved. Brahmā predicts sonbirth when sins are destroyed; the father trembles and asks another remedy.
narrative_events.outcome: Unintentional-vow merit and royal rebirth are described with a fundamental referent gap.
